title: Initial Release
description: Tool declaration block for .void files — mark an existing request as a named, typed capability an AI agent can call directly.

Added: Tool block (/tool) with identity (name/title/description/annotations), a parameters table (agent-supplied vs environment-only source), and a verification policy (verifies rows with role/cadence/mode, plus a per-request on-failure)

onFailure is per verification request, not one tool-wide setting — each entry decides its own consequence (withdraw the tool, or keep it flagged degraded) when it fails; the most conservative failed entry wins when they disagree

Dynamic MCP serving — a verified tool is registered as a real, individually-named/described/typed MCP tool by @voiden/mcp and voiden-runner mcp serve, alongside the 4 generic run/list/write tools every project already gets. A failing tool is withdrawn by default, or served with a degraded note if onFailure: advertise-degraded
Manual enabled override on the tool block — add or remove it from the served set regardless of verification state

Cross-file request/verify references (the /tool block's "attach a request" file picker, and a verify row's optional file override) save a path relative to the referencing file's own project, resolved the same way on read — so the reference survives being cloned to a different machine or opened outside whatever project happens to be active in the sidebar
Environment-sourced params resolve from the project's .voiden/env-public.yaml / env-private.yaml when it has exactly one environment defined, not just the server process's own OS environment
A verify entry (or a tool's own request) targeting a file with no request-separators — i.e. just one request, nothing to disambiguate — no longer needs its sectionLabel to match anything
voiden-runner tool list — discovers every /tool block across a project
voiden-runner tool verify — runs each tool's verification requests and reports verified/unverified/failing, with --cadence filtering and --json/--write output modes
voiden-runner mcp serve [--http] [--check] — serves a project live over MCP (stdio or streamable-HTTP), or reports served/withdrawn/degraded/excluded without starting a session

Load-time structural validation (unbound/unresolved placeholders, dangling verification references, duplicate tool names, read-only tools on mutating requests) — a tool with any of these is excluded from the served set, reported separately from a verification failure
